newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures close with strong gains.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures close with strong gains.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures closed with strong gains and near the highest levels of the session set in late dealings.
A late recovery in Nasdaq stocks, which had been sharply lower most of the session, prompted buying in index futures that sent contracts higher late, traders said.
"It was quiet before then, but it couldn't rally because Nasdaq was lower," said one S&P 500 trader on the floor of the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.

Trade had been nervous during the day at the start of the meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee. Losses in the Nasdaq also made traders wary, but resiliency in the bond market after an initial fall there limited selling interest in index futures, traders said.
The late rally pushed March S&P 500s above chart resistance near 791.00, triggering buy stops that fueled the advance, traders also said.
The advance was orderly, however, and premiums stayed fairly close the theoretical fair values, so arbitragers had little opportunity to execute programs, they said.
The March S&P premium widened to about 4.90 points late, but "by the time we got that rich a premium, the cash was already closed," the floor trader said.
Nikkei 225 stock index futures were fairly quiet throughout the day, with light dealer orders on both sides of the market, and the nearby contract ended unchanged for the day.

At the close, March S&P 500s were up 3.95 points at 793.70, Nasdaq 100s rose 0.75 to 924.75, Russell 2000s were unchanged at 370.10, Value Line futures were up 1.10 points to 709.90, Nikkei 225 index futures were unchanged at 18,340.0 and Midcap 400s rose 0.10 point to 266.15.
